0.content: After Xiuhcoatl's death, Ronova showed Xbalanque the Abyss that would come. He used the divine throne to ask for her power over death. The rules she first wrote into the Night Kingdom were not enough for him, and he made her offer more. She warned that if the wielder failed to overcome the fear of death, innocent lives would pay the price. He answered that Natlan would bow neither to the Abyss nor to her rules. She agreed, as long as the deal stayed secret, and promised to claim that "that treacherous Xbalanque" had stolen her power. Mavuika later used this power against the Abyss, and Ronova came to claim payment in 5.3. Xbalanque's side bet won him one day in the living world, which he collected in 5.3.

1.content: Xbalanque led humanity against the Pyro Dragon Sovereign in what legend places at the Great Volcano of Tollan. Kukulkan says the dragon used one eye to watch over and anchor reality, and that this eye was its only weakness. Xbalanque struck it, and dragon and man fell from a great height together. He died, then rose from the dragon's heart wreathed in flame as Pyro Archon. The eye split into the two Golden Entreaties. He and Kukulkan each kept one and swore to keep peace between humans and dragons.

2.content: Xbalanque did not win alone. Item texts name a band of heroes around him. Lianca joined because he wanted equality for the weak. Och-Kan had mastered the dragons' golden script. Ixquieh lured enemies into traps with Phlogiston. Ahpub fought dragons in mid-air. Maghan played the flute badly, and Uenuku complained about it. After one raid, by the fire, Xbalanque settled their argument over the best weapon and promised Och-Kan a sword forged from dragon materials. He enjoyed throwing absurd questions at bystanders, a habit Och-Kan found aggravating.

3.comment: Xbalanque: The one-day return (As the Blazing Sun)
3.content: After the Abyss was purged, the Wayob told Citlali that Xbalanque would return. He woke in the body of Mausau, a sickly tribal boy. He entered the Pilgrimage tournament and dropped out before the last 32. Mavuika found him and he explained his bet with Ronova. In a spirit arena created from his soul, they fought a duel for as long as one brazier stayed lit, and he narrowly lost. He offered her his remaining life force to bring back someone she missed. She refused, as he had expected, and he passed on messages from her family and comrades in the Night Kingdom. After a flamestrider ride past Ochkanatlan and the People of the Springs, he thanked them and left at sunset. Mausau woke inspired to train for the next Pilgrimage.

4.comment: Xbalanque: Kiongozi, the first Ancient Name
4.content: Kiongozi ("Leader") is Xbalanque's Ancient Name, the first one, in the words of A Thousand Blazing Suns. He asked the Lord of the Night to record it. Over many generations it passed down to Mavuika. Xbalanque decided that the strength built up through this inheritance was why she beat him.

5.content: Och-Kan was half-dragon. Xbalanque showed him compassion, and Och-Kan devoted himself to him and came to think of himself as Xbalanque's "most perfect weapon". He swore to make a realm for humans alone. After Xbalanque entered the Sacred Flame, Och-Kan ruled Ochkanatlan. He believed Xbalanque should remain the only god and broke the commandments of peace with the dragons. In the 7.0 notes, the Belyi Tsar calls Och-Kan the "Sacred Lord" whom Fate had anointed and says Xbalanque took that role from him.
